analysis.title: GS Materials - Nov 4...Copper shorts in more supply cuts, Gold bounce (be-basing?), S232 ask, IVN guidance cut, MT ask tomorrow, GLEN oppty, Oil and Utilities
key_insights: Desk expects copper to be the first ask under Section 232 after the midterms. The President can impose tariffs by executive order without the Senate or House. The investigation report was submitted June 30, 2025 and found copper imports threaten national security. It recommended immediate tariffs on semi-finished copper and copper-intensive derivatives, possible phased tariffs on refined copper, scrap export controls and domestic sourcing mandates.
GS Global Investment Research (GIR) outlined yesterday that tariffs are likely to go up, not down.

Copper opened sharply lower after two heavy selling days. Chinese open interest rose 5% on a $200 move lower, which the desk reads as shorts adding. Short-term CTAs in the West are flat to short. The desk sees $14,100/t as a level where these shorts could cover.

The desk views copper as a supply story that is getting stronger, and an inventory story that is increasingly critical for China. The top story yesterday was Congo's probe of illegal mining after seizing copper and cobalt.
Gold open interest rose 1% with longs adding. The desk calls positioning down the middle and says the narrative is lockdown risk and 'debasement' returning to common use.

Oil view from the trading desk: overnight results make a return to war less likely, though a longer blockade is possible. The desk cites political pressure on Hegseth and says Trump needs a win. It still thinks cool heads prevail given involvement from Russia and China.

Utilities: a Democratic sweep is positive for renewables, with the strongest reads in EDP/EDPR (repowering), SLR (solar), VWS, NDX1 and Orsted. A Texas flip to blue raises Washington overhang risk, which the desk expects to be taken negatively for ENR and GEV at first.
The desk sees a tactical long into the ENR capital markets day (CMD) next week. GS hosts ENR after the CMD.

The desk sees utilities in a dangerous area. The SX6P is back at range highs and almost overbought. De-escalation in the Middle East should bring rotation away from utilities, and escalation brings rates risk.

IVN.CN missed on costs (C1 $3.00/lb vs consensus 2.86) and realized price ($6.15 vs consensus 6.40). It cut 2027 copper guidance to 300-350kt from 380-420kt, a midpoint cut of 75kt from 2027 balances. 2027 cost guidance rose to $2.50-3.00 from $2.10-2.50 and capex was trimmed to $1.1-1.2bn from $1.1-1.4bn. An updated Kamoa-Kakula life-of-mine plan comes in March 2027.
The desk says the market expected the IVN reset, and sees value at 200kt of copper for under $10bn EV. It suggests BHP should look at IVN and notes a Chinese JV partner comes with the asset.

Ramaco (RAMACO) 3Q26 revenue beat on higher volumes but earnings missed on higher costs. Management cut FY2026 production and sales guidance, raised the cash cost outlook, and pushed construction of the Brook Mine pilot plant to 2H27 from 1H27. GS stays Neutral.

Ramaco management cited the Aus PLV forward curve at about $255/ton for 2027, and about 600k tons of excess inventory as a roughly $75mn working capital tailwind through mid-2027. 4Q26 adjusted EBITDA is expected to exceed the roughly $7mn generated year to date. Capex guidance rose to $97-102mn from $92-97mn.

MT.NA published Q3 consensus EBITDA of $1.97bn, while the 28-day best estimate on Bloomberg fell to $1.85bn. The desk cites friction from Ukraine war damage, Liberia iron ore, compressed EU spreads and the Mexico fire. The balance sheet may drift above $10bn on working capital. The desk likes US and India, and notes Brazil is good and the buyback is running.
MT.NA 2027 consensus EBITDA is $10.7bn, which the desk says needs to pick up given the current run rate. The desk expects a MT ask tomorrow.
GLEN trades at 505p versus the desk's 650p. The desk says the market sees it as fitting no category, a consensus long is being unwound, and major asset sales are coming.

China midday wrap: choppy session with lower turnover, support from state funds (NT) continuing, indices around flat, growth outperforming value, hard tech and Physical AI rebounding while optical names weakened and property and cyclicals fell.
